Safe (0 to 53 ppb): Service Car Engines Regularly: Keep ignition and fuel injection systems clean to minimize nitrogen oxide exhaust.
Choose Fuel-Efficient Transport: Opt for hybrid or electric vehicles when upgrading personal transportation.
Use Range Hoods Consistently: Always turn on kitchen ventilation fans when cooking with gas burners.
Support Active Mobility: Walk or bike for local errands to avoid cold-starting fossil-fuel engines.
Optimize Home Heating: Maintain efficient boiler and furnace settings to reduce fossil-fuel combustion volume.
Plant Highway Buffer Trees: Grow dense evergreen shrubs near roadways to absorb localized gaseous emissions.
Limit Unnecessary Driving: Combine weekly trips into streamlined travel loops.
Organize Clean Commute Campaigns: Encourage workplace carpooling and transit pass programs.
Advocate for Electric Transit Fleets: Support municipal investments in zero-emission electric buses.
Participate in Urban Planning Reviews: Support zoning policies that buffer residential areas from heavy freight corridors.
Moderate (54 to 100 ppb): Carpool During Rush Hours: Share rides with coworkers to reduce total vehicle density on congested commuting routes.
Avoid Heavy Traffic Corridors: Choose alternate walking or cycling paths away from major truck freight routes.
Switch to Induction Cooking: Minimize indoor gas stove usage during periods of elevated regional smog.
Set Vehicle Ventilation to Recirculate: Prevent outside exhaust fumes from entering your car cabin in traffic jams.
Delay Non-Essential Commutes: Shift flexible work tasks outside peak morning and evening rush hours.
Maintain Clean Air Filters: Ensure home HVAC and vehicle cabin air filters are fresh and well-maintained.
Avoid Roadside Exercise: Move jogging and cycling routes away from busy urban streets and highways.
Establish School No-Idling Zones: Organize parent-teacher groups to ban engine idling during student drop-off windows.
Promote Flexible Work Hours: Encourage employers to offer staggered start times to flatten rush-hour traffic spikes.
Advocate for Truck Route Restrictions: Petition city councils to restrict heavy diesel freight traffic during peak smog hours.
Dangerous (101+ ppb): Postpone All Discretionary Driving: Stay off the roads during peak congestion periods to avoid severe exposure.
Seal Homes Against Traffic Exhaust: Keep windows closed tight if living adjacent to major highways or industrial plants.
Wear N95/P100 Masks Outdoors: Protect airways from heavy combustion particulate and gas mixes if going outside.
Run Indoor Air Filtration: Keep HEPA and carbon filters running continuously in primary living spaces.
Avoid Outdoor Physical Exertion: Prevent deep lung strain by cancelling all outdoor sports and physical labor.
Use Recirculation Mode Exclusively: Lock vehicle climate controls to internal air recirculation when commuting.
Stay Away from Industrial Zones: Avoid travel near power plants, refineries, and heavy freight depots.
Issue Emergency Traffic Advisories: Coordinate with local agencies to restrict non-essential commercial traffic.
Implement School Recess Restrictions: Mandate indoor-only breaks and activities for all local schools.
Deploy Mobile Air Quality Monitoring: Organize community health checks near major pollution choke points.
